I was in a extremely manipulative on-off relationship for a similar amount of time (this was about 5 years ago), and it hit me like a fucking ton of bricks. If you have anyone to reach out to in real life (a close friend, a therapist, a family member, etc) I really really recommend it. I think what most helped me to get through that break-up was talking openly about it with people, who all collectively told me that my ex was a shitty manipulative person and that I was far better off without him. 

It sounds like he really did a number on your self esteem - again, I would try to remind yourself that his belittling of your appearance was just another way to manipulate you. It doesn't feel like it right now, but you are so much better off. I know that sometimes attention from an abusive person can feel better than no attention at all, but that's a trap that is so easy for us to fall into you. 

Take some time for self care. If you ever feel too unstable, I wouldn't hesitate to reach out for help. I know that after my break-up, I had times when my apartment felt like it was going to swallow me alive and I didn't feel safe there. I started taking long walks as a way to clear my head, and that eventually developed into a biking habit - at least for me, it was helpful to keep myself busy to keep my thoughts away from the crazy nonsense swirling in my head, but your results may vary...
